eligibility: Named Graphalgo family with described hash-gated activation, encrypted archive execution, Slack and Ethereum command channels. The linked primary report supplies paths, commands, file hashes, a public key and contract address.

extraction.saved_text: Only headline and summary; full HTML retrieved to article.html and text to article-full.txt.
extraction.code: Main article contains no code blocks. Linked primary analysis system-report Go code extracted to aikido-code.txt.
extraction.images: Primary figures 0-3 inspected: C2 flow diagram, timeline and two fake ecosystem screenshots. Main article hero is figure-4.png.

sample_provenance: All three feed samples are behavioral reconstructions; no sample was executed. AES-GCM mode and nonce-prefix framing are illustrative implementation choices: the report specifies AES but not its mode or byte framing. Credentials and keys are supplied by callers, not recovered live secrets.
reconstruction_limits: No attempt to fabricate the unknown Terraform input preimage, encrypted path, wallet key, Slack bot token or ECDH derivation details.
Go contract JSON decoder out-parameters are not tracked by source flow. Its verdict states contract/decryption/linked-Open-to-Node co-occurrence, not proven complete network-to-exec flow.
JavaScript for-of element bindings are unresolved by current flow analysis; the variant uses the latest history message during repeated polls.
No credential theft claimed: the article discusses potential cloud access, without showing credential-stealing code.

contract.note: Diagram publishes the client public key; the prose once says private key. No detector infers private-key leakage from this inconsistency.

packages.scope: All versions explicitly specified for the four provider/module indicators by the primary report; @* preserves that stated scope and is not an exact fetchable version. No exact versions were invented.
packages.missing_version: modern-events is a historical malicious npm package named by the primary report with no version or range. Name-only line retained in PURLS.
packages.distribution: The report identifies malicious provider and Go module distributions, not swapped release assets of otherwise clean modules.
packages.excluded: kreuzwerker/docker and kreunzwerker are comparison/upstream names; the fake-site image logger command does not establish malicious package contents.

network.workspace_note: Slack workspace names identify attacker-controlled infrastructure but are not directly contacted by the malware. mediumstar is explicitly historical.
network.excluded_shared_note: Public Slack API is the transport, not malicious identity. No IP address is supplied.

coverage_changes: Removed comment/prose-capable contract-task-method-name and the method-name-gated execution composite. Contract and Slack convictions now require actual GCM Open plus an Open result passed to Node source.
Broadened the existing decryption-derived eval atom to Web Crypto and TextDecoder; renamed it and updated both consumers instead of exceeding the direct-eval leaf budget.
HTTP-origin and crypto-origin predicates must match at the same eval offset (near_bytes=1). Only the ciphertext argument of subtle.decrypt propagates HTTP provenance; key-only data does not.
Narrowed generic fetch/eval and host-profile/POST convictions with linked HTTP provenance and encrypted command-agent context respectively.
Inline Go interpreter observation now requires the executable and its inline source flag; node --version and shell commands no longer imply inline evaluation.
Gated archive loader now requires actual GCM Open, file output and a Go toolchain command. Releasing a toolchain alone is no longer a suspicious supply-chain verdict.
Relocated Go toolchain child-command syntax from create/compile to create/subprocess, and child wait-ownership release to control/wait. No new leaf directories were needed.

External fetch-to-eval alone has suspicious received-code semantics in remote-command/dispatch; exact generic consumers updated. The old hostile fetch/eval correlator now additionally requires the existing WebExtension script-injection capability, preserving a pre-existing extension callback fixture without convicting ordinary fetch/eval co-occurrence. This is a validation-regression correction, not behavior attributed to Graphalgo.

validation.samples: Go agent: 3 hostile. JavaScript agent: 2 hostile. Provider loader: 1 hostile + 1 suspicious. All feed samples met their tier floors on the initial and subsequent scans.
validation.facts: go-facts.json, loader-facts.json and js-final-facts.json contain all cleave facts views. Payload bytes are acquired dynamically: no embedded ciphertext was invented to force decoded-string matches.
validation.controls: Eight controls: unrelated crypto/execution, telemetry, comments, toolchain release without concealment, key-only fetch, plaintext fetch/eval, and separate eval sites. All passed.
